newsitem.title: GERMANY: German savings, farmers banks welcome M3 target.
newsitem.headline: German savings, farmers banks welcome M3 target.

text.p: Germany's savings and farmers bank associations on Thursday both welcomed the Bundesbank's move to set a tighter two-year target corridor for money supply growth in the runup to European monetary union.
The association of popular and agricultural banks (BVR) said the decision marked a "decisive continuation of stability oriented policies" which had helped deliver low inflation.
Meanwhile, the savings banks association (DSGV) said the Bundesbank had set a strong anti-inflation signal even though price pressures were currently weak.
The DSGV also said it supported the Bundesbank's determination to make money supply a key element of monetary policy at the planned European Central Bank after the single currency's launch in 1999.
The Bundesbank said earlier it was tightening its target corridor for growth in M3 money supply to 3.5-6.5 percent, but left open the option to revise that target in a year's time.
